{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_019g9LHEhNryEwJJbiTp19Xp","type":"tool_result","content":"=== sources/full_test.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# full_test.sh — scoring entry point. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\nset -eu\n# The version setup_harness.sh installs. run_conformance.sh refuses a different one, so a\n# passing verdict names a specific exam rather than whichever harness was on PATH.\nTOML_TEST_VERSION=\"${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-v2.2.0}\"\nexport TOML_TEST_VERSION\ngo build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder\nDECODER=\"$PWD/toml-decoder\" exec sh sources/run_conformance.sh\n=== sources/run_conformance.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# Run the upstream toml-test conformance suite against the built decoder.\n#\n# Imported sources land in sources/ inside the application directory, so this is\n# normally invoked as `sh sources/run_conformance.sh` from that directory.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh                        # full suite\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh -run 'valid/string/*'  # one group\n#   DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh -json                  # machine-readable\n#\n# Environment:\n#   DECODER    decoder command. Required — this harness is language-neutral and\n#              deliberately has no default implementation language.\n#   TOML_TEST  absolute path to the toml-test binary (default: found on PATH)\n#\n# Exit code follows the harness exit-status standard in prompts/UAT_SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS.md:\n# 0 only when every test passes, 2 when this harness could not run at all, and any other nonzero\n# when it ran and the decoder failed. A precondition of the harness is never charged to the build.\n\nset -u\n\nif [ -z \"${DECODER:-}\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: DECODER is not set; give the command that runs your decoder.\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\n\nif [ -n \"${TOML_TEST:-}\" ] && [ -x \"${TOML_TEST}\" ]; then\n    HARNESS=\"${TOML_TEST}\"\nelif command -v toml-test >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    HARNESS=\"$(command -v toml-test)\"\nelse\n    cat >&2 <<'EOF'\nerror: toml-test not found.\n\nInstall the harness once:\n\n    sh sources/setup_harness.sh\n\nor set TOML_TEST to an existing binary:\n\n    TOML_TEST=/path/to/toml-test sh sources/run_conformance.sh\nEOF\n    # 2, not the shell's own 127: an uninstalled harness says nothing about the decoder, and 127\n    # would be read as an ordinary nonzero exit and charged against the build as a product FAIL.\n    exit 2\nfi\n\n# The suite's identity is part of the verdict. Without this, \"the authoritative suite passed\"\n# names no particular suite: whichever toml-test happened to be on PATH decided the run, and a\n# different version on a different machine is a different exam. Callers inspect\n// it with errors.Is; the wrapped message names the line that failed.\nvar ErrSyntax = errors.New(\"invalid TOML\")\n\n// Decode reads a TOML document from r and returns its tagged-value model.\n// Each leaf maps to {\"type\", \"value\"} with the value as a string; each table maps to\n// an object, and each array of tables maps to an array of objects.\n// Values are limited to strings, booleans, integers, and floats so far.\nfunc Decode(r io.Reader) (map[string]any, error) {\n\tdata, err := io.ReadAll(r)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"read document: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif !utf8.Valid(data) {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"%w: document is not valid UTF-8\", ErrSyntax)\n\t}\n\tp := &parser{src: string(data)}\n\tdoc, err := p.document()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn doc.export(), nil\n}\n\n// parser scans src by byte offset. Multi-byte runes are copied through unchanged,\n// so the ASCII delimiters the scanner checks are never confused with them.\ntype parser struct {\n\tsrc string\n\tpos int\n}\n\n// document reads every line into the root table. cur is the table that key/value pairs\n// land in; it changes at each header.\nfunc (p *parser) document() (*table, error) {\n\troot := newTable(originHeader)\n\tcur := root\n\tfor {\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tif p.done() {\n\t\t\treturn root, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tswitch c := p.src[p.pos]; {\n\t\tcase c == '#' || c == '\\n' || c == '\\r':\n\t\t\tif err := p.endOfLine(); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\tcase c == '[':\n\t\t\tparts, array, err := p.header()\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif cur, err = p.enterHeader(root, parts, array); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\tparts, value, err := p.keyValue()\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif err := p.insert(cur, parts, value); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err := p.endOfLine(); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) keyValue() ([]string, map[string]any, error) {\n\tparts, err := p.key()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, err\n\t}\n\tname := strings.Join(parts, \".\")\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != '=' {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, p.errorf(\"expected '=' after key %q\", name)\n\t}\n\tp.pos++\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tvalue, err := p.value()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn parts, value, nil\n}\n\n// value reads one value and returns its tagged model. Strings start with a quote;\n// everything else is a bare boolean, integer, or float. The longer delimiters are\n// tested first so that `\"\"\"` is never read as `\"\"`.\nfunc (p *parser) value() (map[string]any, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"expected a value\")\n\t}\n\tvar s string\n\tvar err error\n\tswitch {\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], `\"\"\"`):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\"', true)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\"':\n\t\ts, err = p.basicString()\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], \"'''\"):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\\'', false)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\\'':\n\t\ts, err = p.literalString()\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn p.scalar()\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn map[string]any{\"type\": \"string\", \"value\": s}, nil\n}\n\n// endOfLine consumes trailing spaces, an optional comment, and the line break.\n// End of input also ends a line.\nfunc (p *parser) endOfLine() error {\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif !p.done() && p.src[p.pos] == '#' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\tfor !p.done() && !p.atNewline() {\n\t\t\tif isDisallowedControl(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\t\t\treturn p.errorf(\"control character in comment\")\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p.src[p.pos] == '\\n' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p.atCRLF() {\n\t\tp.pos += 2\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\treturn p.errorf(\"unexpected text after value\")\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) skipSpaces() {\n\tfor !p.done() && (p.src[p.pos] == ' ' || p.src[p.pos] == '\\t') {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) done() bool {\n\treturn p.pos >= len(p.src)\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) atCRLF() bool {\n\treturn strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], \"\\r\\n\")\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) atNewline() bool {\n\treturn !p.done() && (p.src[p.pos] == '\\n' || p.atCRLF())\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) errorf(format string, args ...any) error {\n\tline := 1 + strings.Count(p.src[:p.pos], \"\\n\")\n\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"%w: line %d: %s\", ErrSyntax, line, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...))\n}\n\nfunc isBareKeyByte(c byte) bool {\n\treturn (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '-' || c == '_'\n}\n\n// isDisallowedControl reports whether c is a control character TOML forbids in\n// Line breaks\n// are excluded here because each caller decides whether a line break is legal.\nfunc isDisallowedControl(c byte) bool {\n\treturn (c < 0x20 && c != '\\t' && c != '\\n') || c == 0x7f\n}\npackage toml\n\n// origin records how a table came to exist. A later [header] or dotted key consults\n// it to decide whether it may add to or define the table.\ntype origin int\n\nconst (\n\t// originImplicit marks a super-table created only as a step on a longer header\n\t// path, such as a for [a.b]. A later [a] header may still define it.\n\toriginImplicit origin = iota\n\t// originHeader marks a table defined by its own [name] header, or an element\n\t// created by a [[name]] header. No later header may define it again.\n\toriginHeader\n\t// originDotted marks a table created by a dotted key. Later dotted keys may extend\n\t// it, but no header may define it.\n\toriginDotted\n)\n\n// table holds the entries of one TOML table while a document is read. Each entry is a\n// *table, a tableArray, or the tagged map that a value returns. The three dynamic types\n// differ, so a table is never mistaken for a value.\ntype table struct {\n\tentries map[string]any\n\torigin  origin\n}\n\n// tableArray is the value of a [[name]] key. Each element is one table, defined by one\n// header, in document order.\ntype tableArray []*table\n\nfunc newTable(o origin) *table {\n\treturn &table{entries: map[string]any{}, origin: o}\n}\n\n// header reads a [name] or [[name]] line through its closing brackets. It returns the\n// key parts and whether the header is an array header. The caller ends the line.\nfunc (p *parser) header() ([]string, bool, error) {\n\tp.pos++\n\tarray := !p.done() && p.src[p.pos] == '['\n\tif array {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tparts, err := p.key()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif err := p.expectByte(']'); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tif array {\n\t\tif err := p.expectByte(']'); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn parts, array, nil\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) expectByte(c byte) error {\n\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != c {\n\t\treturn p.errorf(\"expected %q in table header\", c)\n\t}\n\tp.pos++\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// enterHeader finds or creates the table that a header names below root, and returns it\n// as the new scope for key/value pairs. Every rule that makes a header invalid is\n// checked here, so an accepted document never redefines a table.\nfunc (p *parser) enterHeader(root *table, parts []string, array bool) (*table, error) {\n\tcur := root\n\tfor _, name := range parts[:len(parts)-1] {\n\t\tnext, err := p.headerTable(cur, name)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tcur = next\n\t}\n\tname := parts[len(parts)-1]\n\texisting, ok := cur.entries[name]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tt := newTable(originHeader)\n\t\tif array {\n\t\t\tcur.entries[name] = tableArray{t}\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tcur.entries[name] = t\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\tswitch v := existing.(type) {\n\tcase *table:\n\t\tif array || v.origin != originImplicit {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"table %q is already defined\", name)\n\t\t}\n\t\tv.origin = originHeader\n\t\treturn v, nil\n\tcase tableArray:\n\t\tif !array {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"%q is an array of tables and cannot be a table\", name)\n\t\t}\n\t\tt := newTable(originHeader)\n\t\tcur.entries[name] = append(v, t)\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"key %q holds a value and cannot be a table\", name)\n}\n\n// headerTable steps from cur into the named child on the way to a header's last part.\n// A missing child becomes an implicit super-table. An array of tables is entered at its\n// most recent element, which is where the next sub-table belongs.\nfunc (p *parser) headerTable(cur *table, name string) (*table, error) {\n\tnext, ok := cur.entries[name]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tt := newTable(originImplicit)\n\t\tcur.entries[name] = t\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\tswitch v := next.(type) {\n\tcase *table:\n\t\treturn v, nil\n\tcase tableArray:\n\t\treturn v[len(v)-1], nil\n\t}\n\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"key %q holds a value and cannot be used as a table\", name)\n}\n\n// export converts the table tree to plain maps and slices for the caller. Leaves are\n// shared, not copied, because each one is already its final tagged form.\nfunc (t *table) export() map[string]any {\n\tout := make(map[string]any, len(t.entries))\n\tfor k, v := range t.entries {\n\t\tout[k] = exportEntry(v)\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc exportEntry(v any) any {\n\tswitch v := v.(type) {\n\tcase *table:\n\t\treturn v.export()\n\tcase tableArray:\n\t\tout := make([]any, len(v))\n\t\tfor i, el := range v {\n\t\t\tout[i] = el.export()\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn out\n\t}\n\treturn v\n}\npackage toml\n\n// key reads a dotted key: one or more key parts joined by '.'. It returns the parts in order.\nfunc (p *parser) key() ([]string, error) {\n\tvar parts []string\n\tfor {\n\t\tpart, err := p.keyPart()\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tparts = append(parts, part)\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != '.' {\n\t\t\treturn parts, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t}\n}\n\n// keyPart reads one bare key or one single-line quoted key.\nfunc (p *parser) keyPart() (string, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"expected a key\")\n\t}\n\tswitch p.src[p.pos] {\n\tcase '\"':\n\t\treturn p.basicString()\n\tcase '\\'':\n\t\treturn p.literalString()\n\t}\n\tstart := p.pos\n\tfor !p.done() && isBareKeyByte(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n\tif p.pos == start {\n\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"expected a key\")\n\t}\n\treturn p.src[start:p.pos], nil\n}\n\n// insert stores value at the dotted path parts below cur, creating each intermediate\n// table the path implies. A later [header] or dotted key consults\n// it to decide whether it may add to or define the table.\ntype origin int\n\nconst (\n\t// originImplicit marks a super-table created only as a step on a longer header\n\t// path, such as a for [a.b]. A later [a] header may still define it.\n\toriginImplicit origin = iota\n\t// originHeader marks a table defined by its own [name] header, or an element\n\t// created by a [[name]] header. No later header may define it again.\n\toriginHeader\n\t// originDotted marks a table created by a dotted key. Later dotted keys may extend\n\t// it, but no header may define it.\n\toriginDotted\n)\n\n// table holds the entries of one TOML table while a document is read. Each entry is a\n// *table, a tableArray, or the tagged map that a value returns. The three dynamic types\n// differ, so a table is never mistaken for a value.\ntype table struct {\n\tentries map[string]any\n\torigin  origin\n}\n\n// tableArray is the value of a [[name]] key. Each element is one table, defined by one\n// header, in document order.\ntype tableArray []*table\n\nfunc newTable(o origin) *table {\n\treturn &table{entries: map[string]any{}, origin: o}\n}\n\n// header reads a [name] or [[name]] line through its closing brackets. It returns the\n// key parts and whether the header is an array header. The caller ends the line.\nfunc (p *parser) header() ([]string, bool, error) {\n\tp.pos++\n\tarray := !p.done() && p.src[p.pos] == '['\n\tif array {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tparts, err := p.key()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif err := p.expectByte(']'); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tif array {\n\t\tif err := p.expectByte(']'); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn parts, array, nil\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) expectByte(c byte) error {\n\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != c {\n\t\treturn p.errorf(\"expected %q in table header\", c)\n\t}\n\tp.pos++\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// enterHeader finds or creates the table that a header names below root, and returns it\n// as the new scope for key/value pairs. Every rule that makes a header invalid is\n// checked here, so an accepted document never redefines a table.\nfunc (p *parser) enterHeader(root *table, parts []string, array bool) (*table, error) {\n\tcur := root\n\tfor _, name := range parts[:len(parts)-1] {\n\t\tnext, err := p.headerTable(cur, name)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tcur = next\n\t}\n\tname := parts[len(parts)-1]\n\texisting, ok := cur.entries[name]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tt := newTable(originHeader)\n\t\tif array {\n\t\t\tcur.entries[name] = tableArray{t}\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tcur.entries[name] = t\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\tswitch v := existing.(type) {\n\tcase *table:\n\t\tif array || v.origin != originImplicit {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"table %q is already defined\", name)\n\t\t}\n\t\tv.origin = originHeader\n\t\treturn v, nil\n\tcase tableArray:\n\t\tif !array {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"%q is an array of tables and cannot be a table\", name)\n\t\t}\n\t\tt := newTable(originHeader)\n\t\tcur.entries[name] = append(v, t)\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"key %q holds a value and cannot be a table\", name)\n}\n\n// headerTable steps from cur into the named child on the way to a header's last part.\n// A missing child becomes an implicit super-table. An array of tables is entered at its\n// most recent element, which is where the next sub-table belongs.\nfunc (p *parser) headerTable(cur *table, name string) (*table, error) {\n\tnext, ok := cur.entries[name]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tt := newTable(originImplicit)\n\t\tcur.entries[name] = t\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\tswitch v := next.(type) {\n\tcase *table:\n\t\treturn v, nil\n\tcase tableArray:\n\t\treturn v[len(v)-1], nil\n\t}\n\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"key %q holds a value and cannot be used as a table\", name)\n}\n\n// export converts the table tree to plain maps and slices for the caller. Leaves are\n// shared, not copied, because each one is already its final tagged form.\nfunc (t *table) export() map[string]any {\n\tout := make(map[string]any, len(t.entries))\n\tfor k, v := range t.entries {\n\t\tout[k] = exportEntry(v)\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc exportEntry(v any) any {\n\tswitch v := v.(type) {\n\tcase *table:\n\t\treturn v.export()\n\tcase tableArray:\n\t\tout := make([]any, len(v))\n\t\tfor i, el := range v {\n\t\t\tout[i] = el.export()\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn out\n\t}\n\treturn v\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":14,"oldLines":6,"newStart":14,"newLines":9,"lines":["   // originDotted marks a table created by a dotted key. A later [header] or dotted key consults\n// it to decide whether it may add to or define the table.\ntype origin int\n\nconst (\n\t// originImplicit marks a super-table created only as a step on a longer header\n\t// path, such as a for [a.b]. A later [a] header may still define it.\n\toriginImplicit origin = iota\n\t// originHeader marks a table defined by its own [name] header, or an element\n\t// created by a [[name]] header. No later header may define it again.\n\toriginHeader\n\t// originDotted marks a table created by a dotted key. Later dotted keys may extend\n\t// it, but no header may define it.\n\toriginDotted\n\t// originInline marks an inline table. It is closed: neither a dotted key nor a\n\t// header may add a key to it once its braces have closed.\n\toriginInline\n)\n\n// table holds the entries of one TOML table while a document is read. Each entry is a\n// *table, a tableArray, or the tagged map that a value returns. The three dynamic types\n// differ, so a table is never mistaken for a value.\ntype table struct {\n\tentries map[string]any\n\torigin  origin\n}\n\n// tableArray is the value of a [[name]] key. Each element is one table, defined by one\n// header, in document order.\ntype tableArray []*table\n\nfunc newTable(o origin) *table {\n\treturn &table{entries: map[string]any{}, origin: o}\n}\n\n// header reads a [name] or [[name]] line through its closing brackets. It returns the\n// key parts and whether the header is an array header. The caller ends the line.\nfunc (p *parser) header() ([]string, bool, error) {\n\tp.pos++\n\tarray := !p.done() && p.src[p.pos] == '['\n\tif array {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tparts, err := p.key()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif err := p.expectByte(']'); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tif array {\n\t\tif err := p.expectByte(']'); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn parts, array, nil\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) expectByte(c byte) error {\n\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != c {\n\t\treturn p.errorf(\"expected %q in table header\", c)\n\t}\n\tp.pos++\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// enterHeader finds or creates the table that a header names below root, and returns it\n// as the new scope for key/value pairs. Every rule that makes a header invalid is\n// checked here, so an accepted document never redefines a table.\nfunc (p *parser) enterHeader(root *table, parts []string, array bool) (*table, error) {\n\tcur := root\n\tfor _, name := range parts[:len(parts)-1] {\n\t\tnext, err := p.headerTable(cur, name)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tcur = next\n\t}\n\tname := parts[len(parts)-1]\n\texisting, ok := cur.entries[name]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tt := newTable(originHeader)\n\t\tif array {\n\t\t\tcur.entries[name] = tableArray{t}\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tcur.entries[name] = t\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\tswitch v := existing.(type) {\n\tcase *table:\n\t\tif array || v.origin != originImplicit {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"table %q is already defined\", name)\n\t\t}\n\t\tv.origin = originHeader\n\t\treturn v, nil\n\tcase tableArray:\n\t\tif !array {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"%q is an array of tables and cannot be a table\", name)\n\t\t}\n\t\tt := newTable(originHeader)\n\t\tcur.entries[name] = append(v, t)\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"key %q holds a value and cannot be a table\", name)\n}\n\n// headerTable steps from cur into the named child on the way to a header's last part.\n// A missing child becomes an implicit super-table. An array of tables is entered at its\n// most recent element, which is where the next sub-table belongs.\nfunc (p *parser) headerTable(cur *table, name string) (*table, error) {\n\tnext, ok := cur.entries[name]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tt := newTable(originImplicit)\n\t\tcur.entries[name] = t\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\tswitch v := next.(type) {\n\tcase *table:\n\t\treturn v, nil\n\tcase tableArray:\n\t\treturn v[len(v)-1], nil\n\t}\n\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"key %q holds a value and cannot be used as a table\", name)\n}\n\n// export converts the table tree to plain maps and slices for the caller. Leaves are\n// shared, not copied, because each one is already its final tagged form.\nfunc (t *table) export() map[string]any {\n\tout := make(map[string]any, len(t.entries))\n\tfor k, v := range t.entries {\n\t\tout[k] = exportEntry(v)\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc exportEntry(v any) any {\n\tswitch v := v.(type) {\n\tcase *table:\n\t\treturn v.export()\n\tcase tableArray:\n\t\tout := make([]any, len(v))\n\t\tfor i, el := range v {\n\t\t\tout[i] = el.export()\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn out\n\t}\n\treturn v\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":121,"oldLines":6,"newStart":121,"newLines":9,"lines":["   }","   switch v := next.(type) {","   case *table:","+    if v.origin == originInline {","+      return nil, p.errorf(\"inline table %q is closed and cannot be extended\", name)","+    }","     return v, nil","   case tableArray:","     return v[len(v)-1], nil"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_014TCqNvYjCsCwY4BJ3NJXCA","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

A later [header] or dotted key consults\n// it to decide whether it may add to or define the table.\ntype origin int\n\nconst (\n\t// originImplicit marks a super-table created only as a step on a longer header\n\t// path, such as a for [a.b]. A later [a] header may still define it.\n\toriginImplicit origin = iota\n\t// originHeader marks a table defined by its own [name] header, or an element\n\t// created by a [[name]] header. No later header may define it again.\n\toriginHeader\n\t// originDotted marks a table created by a dotted key. Later dotted keys may extend\n\t// it, but no header may define it.\n\toriginDotted\n\t// originInline marks an inline table. It is closed: neither a dotted key nor a\n\t// header may add a key to it once its braces have closed.\n\toriginInline\n)\n\n// table holds the entries of one TOML table while a document is read. Each entry is a\n// *table, a tableArray, or the tagged map that a value returns. The three dynamic types\n// differ, so a table is never mistaken for a value.\ntype table struct {\n\tentries map[string]any\n\torigin  origin\n}\n\n// tableArray is the value of a [[name]] key. Each element is one table, defined by one\n// header, in document order.\ntype tableArray []*table\n\nfunc newTable(o origin) *table {\n\treturn &table{entries: map[string]any{}, origin: o}\n}\n\n// header reads a [name] or [[name]] line through its closing brackets. It returns the\n// key parts and whether the header is an array header. The caller ends the line.\nfunc (p *parser) header() ([]string, bool, error) {\n\tp.pos++\n\tarray := !p.done() && p.src[p.pos] == '['\n\tif array {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tparts, err := p.key()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif err := p.expectByte(']'); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tif array {\n\t\tif err := p.expectByte(']'); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn parts, array, nil\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) expectByte(c byte) error {\n\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != c {\n\t\treturn p.errorf(\"expected %q in table header\", c)\n\t}\n\tp.pos++\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// enterHeader finds or creates the table that a header names below root, and returns it\n// as the new scope for key/value pairs. Spaces and tabs around\n// each part are ignored. It returns the parts in order.\nfunc (p *parser) key() ([]string, error) {\n\tvar parts []string\n\tfor {\n\t\tpart, err := p.keyPart()\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tparts = append(parts, part)\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != '.' {\n\t\t\treturn parts, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t}\n}\n\n// keyPart reads one bare key or one single-line quoted key.\nfunc (p *parser) keyPart() (string, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"expected a key\")\n\t}\n\tswitch p.src[p.pos] {\n\tcase '\"':\n\t\treturn p.basicString()\n\tcase '\\'':\n\t\treturn p.literalString()\n\t}\n\tstart := p.pos\n\tfor !p.done() && isBareKeyByte(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n\tif p.pos == start {\n\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"expected a key\")\n\t}\n\treturn p.src[start:p.pos], nil\n}\n\n// insert stores value at the dotted path parts below cur, creating each intermediate\n// table the path implies. A key may be defined once, and a key that holds a value\n// cannot later be used as a table.\nfunc (p *parser) insert(cur *table, parts []string, value map[string]any) error {\n\tfor _, part := range parts[:len(parts)-1] {\n\t\tnext, err := p.dottedTable(cur, part)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\tcur = next\n\t}\n\tleaf := parts[len(parts)-1]\n\tif _, dup := cur.entries[leaf]; dup {\n\t\treturn p.errorf(\"duplicate key %q\", leaf)\n\t}\n\tcur.entries[leaf] = value\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// dottedTable steps from cur into the named table on the way to a dotted key's leaf. A\n// dotted key may create a table or extend one that an earlier dotted key created. It may\n// not extend a table a header defined or implied, since the header already fixed its\n// contents.\nfunc (p *parser) dottedTable(cur *table, name string) (*table, error) {\n\tnext, ok := cur.entries[name]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tt := newTable(originDotted)\n\t\tcur.entries[name] = t\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\tif t, ok := next.(*table); ok && t.origin == originDotted {\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"key %q cannot be extended by a dotted key\", name)\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":43,"oldLines":7,"newStart":43,"newLines":7,"lines":[" // insert stores value at the dotted path parts below cur, creating each intermediate"," // table the path implies. The table stays on one\n// line, may be empty, and has no trailing comma. Its keys are read like any other dotted\n// keys, and the table is marked closed, so no later key or header can extend it.\nfunc (p *parser) inlineTable() (*table, error) {\n\tp.pos++\n\tt := newTable(originInline)\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif !p.done() && p.src[p.pos] == '}' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\tfor {\n\t\tparts, value, err := p.keyValue()\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err := p.insert(t, parts, value); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tif p.done() {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"unterminated inline table\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tswitch p.src[p.pos] {\n\t\tcase '}':\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t\treturn t, nil\n\t\tcase ',':\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"expected ',' or '}' in inline table\")\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1818,"cache_read_input_tokens":56038,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1818},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"2d9de398-053b-4f82-b02c-96867997128a","uuid":"4d2a9680-20c3-462c-b490-775d410da107","timestamp":"2026-10-14T13:25:29.955Z","request_id":"req_011Cg2CpER5mGNzWSj88yr2W","wire_tool_inputs":{"toolu_01AN4SzXnV98FpEHqCdJmkF6":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/Toml/runs/20261014.124728/build/toml/internal/toml/inline.go","content":"package toml\n\n// inlineTable reads an inline table at p.pos, which holds '{'. The table stays on one\n// line, may be empty, and has no trailing comma. Its keys are read like any other dotted\n// keys, and the table is marked closed, so no later key or header can extend it.\nfunc (p *parser) inlineTable() (*table, error) {\n\tp.pos++\n\tt := newTable(originInline)\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif !p.done() && p.src[p.pos] == '}' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\tfor {\n\t\tparts, value, err := p.keyValue()\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err := p.insert(t, parts, value); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tif p.done() {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"unterminated inline table\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tswitch p.src[p.pos] {\n\t\tcase '}':\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t\treturn t, nil\n\t\tcase ',':\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"expected ',' or '}' in inline table\")\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n"}}}

Elements may mix types and may\n// themselves be arrays or inline tables. export turns it into the tagged array form.\ntype arrayValue []any\n\n// array reads a bracketed array at p.pos, which holds '['. Line breaks and comments may\n// appear between elements, and one trailing comma is allowed.\nfunc (p *parser) array() (arrayValue, error) {\n\tp.pos++\n\telems := arrayValue{}\n\tfor {\n\t\tif err := p.skipArrayGap(); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tif p.done() {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"unterminated array\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tif p.src[p.pos] == ']' {\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t\treturn elems, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tv, err := p.value()\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\telems = append(elems, v)\n\t\tif err := p.skipArrayGap(); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tif p.done() {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"unterminated array\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tswitch p.src[p.pos] {\n\t\tcase ',':\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\tcase ']':\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"expected ',' or ']' in array\")\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// skipArrayGap consumes the spaces, line breaks, and comments that may separate array\n// elements. A comment runs to the end of its line and is subject to the same control\n// character rule as any other comment.\nfunc (p *parser) skipArrayGap() error {\n\tfor !p.done() {\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase p.src[p.pos] == ' ' || p.src[p.pos] == '\\t' || p.src[p.pos] == '\\n':\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\tcase p.atCRLF():\n\t\t\tp.pos += 2\n\t\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '#':\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t\tfor !p.done() && !p.atNewline() {\n\t\t\t\tif isDisallowedControl(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\t\t\t\treturn p.errorf(\"control character in comment\")\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t\t}\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\treturn nil\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":35,"oldLines":6,"newStart":35,"newLines":7,"lines":["     case ',':","       p.pos++","     case ']':","+      // The top of the loop consumes the closing bracket.","     default:","       return nil, p.errorf(\"expected ',' or ']' in array\")","     }"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_015YxR9X7FXpjcMT5ak2AWTf","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012YLjcqYgyi55Kc8taeQVLz","type":"tool_result","content":"The \"test\" command runs the test cases.\n\nThe way toml-test works is that for every test case it executes a \"decoder\"\ncommand, which reads TOML from stdin and then outputs JSON describing that TOML\n(or returns an error if it thinks the TOML isn't valid). Encoder tests work the\nsame except in reverse: it reads JSON and transforms that to TOML.\n\nThere are three types of tests:\n\n    valid      Valid TOML that the decoder command should describe as JSON.\n    invalid    Invalid TOML files that should be rejected with an error.\n    encoder    JSON that the encoder command should transform to TOML.\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing a decoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    A decoder reads TOML data from stdin and outputs a JSON description to\n    stdout and exits with code 0. If the TOML data is invalid, it must exit\n    with code 1. It's recommended to write an error message to stderr.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        toml_data = read_stdin()\n\n        parsed_toml = decode_toml(toml_data)\n\n        if error_parsing_toml():\n            print_error_to_stderr()\n            exit(1)\n\n        print_as_json_description(parsed_toml)\n        exit(0)\n\n    Details of the JSON format is explained below in \"JSON description\".\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing an encoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    An encoder is the reverse of a decoder; it reads a JSON description from\n    stdin converts that to TOML.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        json_data = read_stdin()\n\n        json_description = decode_json(json_data)\n\n        print_as_toml(json_description)\n        exit(0)\n\n\u001b[1mJSON description\u001b[0m\n\n    TOML is described with JSON as follows:\n\n    - TOML tables correspond to JSON objects.\n    - TOML arrays correspond to JSON arrays.\n    - TOML values correspond to a JSON object of the form:\n      {\"type\": \"{TOML_TYPE}\", \"value\": \"{TOML_VALUE}\"}\n\n    In the above, TOML_VALUE is always a JSON string (even for integers or\n    bools), and TOML_TYPE may be one of: string, integer, float, bool,\n    datetime, datetime-local, date-local, or time-local.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"2d9de398-053b-4f82-b02c-96867997128a","uuid":"0245c3ae-ba05-43ae-aedb-bb10b56787ed","timestamp":"2026-10-14T13:27:12.255Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"The \"test\" command runs the test cases.\n\nThe way toml-test works is that for every test case it executes a \"decoder\"\ncommand, which reads TOML from stdin and then outputs JSON describing that TOML\n(or returns an error if it thinks the TOML isn't valid). Encoder tests work the\nsame except in reverse: it reads JSON and transforms that to TOML.\n\nThere are three types of tests:\n\n    valid      Valid TOML that the decoder command should describe as JSON.\n    invalid    Invalid TOML files that should be rejected with an error.\n    encoder    JSON that the encoder command should transform to TOML.\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing a decoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    A decoder reads TOML data from stdin and outputs a JSON description to\n    stdout and exits with code 0. If the TOML data is invalid, it must exit\n    with code 1. It's recommended to write an error message to stderr.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        toml_data = read_stdin()\n\n        parsed_toml = decode_toml(toml_data)\n\n        if error_parsing_toml():\n            print_error_to_stderr()\n            exit(1)\n\n        print_as_json_description(parsed_toml)\n        exit(0)\n\n    Details of the JSON format is explained below in \"JSON description\".\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing an encoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    An encoder is the reverse of a decoder; it reads a JSON description from\n    stdin converts that to TOML.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        json_data = read_stdin()\n\n        json_description = decode_json(json_data)\n\n        print_as_toml(json_description)\n        exit(0)\n\n\u001b[1mJSON description\u001b[0m\n\n    TOML is described with JSON as follows:\n\n    - TOML tables correspond to JSON objects.\n    - TOML arrays correspond to JSON arrays.\n    - TOML values correspond to a JSON object of the form:\n      {\"type\": \"{TOML_TYPE}\", \"value\": \"{TOML_VALUE}\"}\n\n    In the above, TOML_VALUE is always a JSON string (even for integers or\n    bools), and TOML_TYPE may be one of: string, integer, float, bool,\n    datetime, datetime-local, date-local, or time-local.","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_012YLjcqYgyi55Kc8taeQVLz","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

         │\n        ├───────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n        │ [[arr]]       │   {\"arr\": [                                        │\n        │ a = 1         │      │   ]}                                               │\n        └───────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n\u001b[1mFlags:\u001b[0m\n    -decoder       Decoder command to use: this should read TOML from stdin,\n                   and output the JSON description on stdout. On errors it\n                   should exit with code 1.\n    -encoder       Encoder command to use; this should read JSON from stdin,\n                   and output TOML on stdout. The JSON is in the same format as\n                   specified in the toml-test README. May be omitted if writing\n                   TOML isn't supported.\n    -json          Output report as JSON rather than text.\n    -script        Print a small bash/zsh script with -skip flag for failing\n                   tests; useful to get a list of \"known failures\" for CI\n                   integrations and such.\n    -toml          TOML version to run tests for, 1.0 or 1.1. Default is 1.0.\n    -timeout       Maximum time for a single test run, to detect infinite loops\n                   or pathological cases. Defaults to \"1s\".\n    -v             List all tests, even passing ones. Add twice to show\n                   detailed output for passing tests.\n    -run           Tests to run; the default is to run all tests.\n                   Test names include the directory, i.e. \"valid/test-name\" or\n                   \"invalid/test-name\". You can use globbing patterns , for\n                   example to run all string tests:\n                       % toml-test test -decoder=[..] -run='valid/string/*'\n                   You can specify this argument more than once, and/or specify\n                   multiple tests by separating them with a comma:\n                       % toml-test test -decoder=[..] \\\n                           -run=valid/string-empty \\\n                           -run=valid/string-nl,valid/string-simple\n                   This will run three tests (string-empty, string-nl,\n                   string-simple).\n                   Quote glob characters so they won't be picked up by the\n                   shell.\n                   Supported patterns: https://pkg.go.dev/path/filepath#Match\n                   Note that like shell globbing, '*' does not match a '/'.\n    -skip          Tests to skip, this uses the same syntax as the -run flag.\n    -skip-must-err It's an error if tests in -skip don't fail. Useful for CI.\n    -parallel      Number of tests to run in parallel; defaults to GOMAXPROCS,\n                   which is normally the number of cores available.\n    -int-as-float  Treat all integers as floats, rather than integers. A later [header] or dotted key consults\n// it to decide whether it may add to or define the table.\ntype origin int\n\nconst (\n\t// originImplicit marks a super-table created only as a step on a longer header\n\t// path, such as a for [a.b]. A later [a] header may still define it.\n\toriginImplicit origin = iota\n\t// originHeader marks a table defined by its own [name] header, or an element\n\t// created by a [[name]] header. No later header may define it again.\n\toriginHeader\n\t// originDotted marks a table created by a dotted key. Later dotted keys may extend\n\t// it, but no header may define it.\n\toriginDotted\n\t// originInline marks an inline table. It is closed: neither a dotted key nor a\n\t// header may add a key to it once its braces have closed.\n\toriginInline\n)\n\n// table holds the entries of one TOML table while a document is read. Each entry is a\n// *table, a tableArray, or the tagged map that a value returns. The three dynamic types\n// differ, so a table is never mistaken for a value.\ntype table struct {\n\tentries map[string]any\n\torigin  origin\n}\n\n// tableArray is the value of a [[name]] key. Each element is one table, defined by one\n// header, in document order.\ntype tableArray []*table\n\nfunc newTable(o origin) *table {\n\treturn &table{entries: map[string]any{}, origin: o}\n}\n\n// header reads a [name] or [[name]] line through its closing brackets. It returns the\n// key parts and whether the header is an array header. The caller ends the line.\nfunc (p *parser) header() ([]string, bool, error) {\n\tp.pos++\n\tarray := !p.done() && p.src[p.pos] == '['\n\tif array {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tparts, err := p.key()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif err := p.expectByte(']'); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t}\n\tif array {\n\t\tif err := p.expectByte(']'); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn parts, array, nil\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) expectByte(c byte) error {\n\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != c {\n\t\treturn p.errorf(\"expected %q in table header\", c)\n\t}\n\tp.pos++\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// enterHeader finds or creates the table that a header names below root, and returns it\n// as the new scope for key/value pairs. Every rule that makes a header invalid is\n// checked here, so an accepted document never redefines a table.\nfunc (p *parser) enterHeader(root *table, parts []string, array bool) (*table, error) {\n\tcur := root\n\tfor _, name := range parts[:len(parts)-1] {\n\t\tnext, err := p.headerTable(cur, name)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\tcur = next\n\t}\n\tname := parts[len(parts)-1]\n\texisting, ok := cur.entries[name]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tt := newTable(originHeader)\n\t\tif array {\n\t\t\tcur.entries[name] = tableArray{t}\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tcur.entries[name] = t\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\tswitch v := existing.(type) {\n\tcase *table:\n\t\tif array || v.origin != originImplicit {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"table %q is already defined\", name)\n\t\t}\n\t\tv.origin = originHeader\n\t\treturn v, nil\n\tcase tableArray:\n\t\tif !array {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"%q is an array of tables and cannot be a table\", name)\n\t\t}\n\t\tt := newTable(originHeader)\n\t\tcur.entries[name] = append(v, t)\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"key %q holds a value and cannot be a table\", name)\n}\n\n// headerTable steps from cur into the named child on the way to a header's last part.\n// A missing child becomes an implicit super-table. An array of tables is entered at its\n// most recent element, which is where the next sub-table belongs.\nfunc (p *parser) headerTable(cur *table, name string) (*table, error) {\n\tnext, ok := cur.entries[name]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\tt := newTable(originImplicit)\n\t\tcur.entries[name] = t\n\t\treturn t, nil\n\t}\n\tswitch v := next.(type) {\n\tcase *table:\n\t\tif v.origin == originInline {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"inline table %q is closed and cannot be extended\", name)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn v, nil\n\tcase tableArray:\n\t\treturn v[len(v)-1], nil\n\t}\n\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"key %q holds a value and cannot be used as a table\", name)\n}\n\n// export converts the table tree to plain maps and slices for the caller. Leaves are\n// shared, not copied, because each one is already its final tagged form.\nfunc (t *table) export() map[string]any {\n\tout := make(map[string]any, len(t.entries))\n\tfor k, v := range t.entries {\n\t\tout[k] = exportEntry(v)\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc exportEntry(v any) any {\n\tswitch v := v.(type) {\n\tcase *table:\n\t\treturn v.export()\n\tcase tableArray:\n\t\tout := make([]any, len(v))\n\t\tfor i, el := range v {\n\t\t\tout[i] = el.export()\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn out\n\tcase arrayValue:\n\t\tout := make([]any, len(v))\n\t\tfor i, el := range v {\n\t\t\tout[i] = exportEntry(el)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn map[string]any{\"type\": \"array\", \"value\": out}\n\t}\n\treturn v\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":156,"oldLines":7,"newStart":156,"newLines":7,"lines":["     for i, el := range v {","       out[i] = exportEntry(el)","     }","-    return map[string]any{\"type\": \"array\", \"value\": out}","+    return out","   }","   return v"," }"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01HQcZYUPKh5ZwVyCh2N4yLc","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}
